blocks.content: Previewing annotation templates lets you catch syntax errors and verify formatting before saving the rule. You can preview using alert data from existing instances or custom test data.
To preview your annotation templates, complete the following steps:
First, ensure your queries have fresh data. Click **Run queries** in section 2 to refresh the query results.

Click **Preview** below the alert condition to generate alert instances from current data.

The preview table shows which series would fire. Each row represents an alert instance with its labels and values—these are the same labels and values your templates will render.

Check the preview results against your template expectations:

| Check | What to look for |
|-------|------------------|
| **Labels present** | Does `$labels.instance` (or your label) appear in the preview? If not, the label isn't in the query result |
| **Values present** | Does `$values.A.Value` show a number? If it shows `NaN`, the query may be a range query (use a Reduce expression) |
| **Template syntax** | If the rendered annotation shows raw `{{ }}` text instead of values, check for typos in variable names |

> **Tip:** If `$labels` is empty, your rule may be using a single-condition query that discards individual labels. Switch to Advanced mode and use Reduce and Threshold expressions, which preserve labels from the original query.
Your annotation templates render correctly. In the next milestone, you'll write a conditional label template.
